analysis.title: Few charts
key_insights: Clients aggressively sold protection into Wednesday's rally, then scrambled to buy it back on Thursday as markets sold off.
The Vol Panic index surged to 9.57 out of 10 on Thursday. The 5% increase was the 3rd largest daily jump ever, and the chart shows the biggest 2-day round trip on record.
GS's AI basket (GSTMTAIP) had its worst one-day performance since Covid on Thursday. The desk describes the move as macro driven, citing exploding ETF volumes.

US-listed ETFs printed $580 billion of notional volume on Thursday, the third largest day in the dataset and 33% of the tape (28% average). On Friday volume was 36% of the tape and dollar volumes ran +65% vs the 20-day average. QQQ set a notional volume record at $86 billion.
US-listed ETF shorts rose 7% on Thursday in the prime books, the largest 1-day increase since March and the third largest in five years, led by shorting in Large Cap Equity ETFs.
Prime data show global equities de-grossing for a 4th straight session (8 of the last 9), though Thursday's pace of risk unwinds was relatively modest.
Global equities saw the largest net selling in two weeks (-1.6 SDs vs 1-year), with long sales outpacing short sales 2.2 to 1.

Global AI stocks (GSXGGLAI constituents) were net sold for a 6th consecutive session (-2.6 SDs 1-year). Hedge fund selling of global AI stocks over a trailing 20 days is the largest in more than five years (-3.0 SDs 5-year).
AI-related volatility has taken over from energy prices as the primary driver of directional yield moves.
Growth and momentum factors sold off while Value outperformed. The Risk Appetite Indicator has fallen significantly over the last month to -0.7 (momentum at -1.2).

GS Global Investment Research argues for strong visibility on US data center construction growth through 2028, backed by 28GW under construction and a $900bn high-confidence pipeline. It raises its 2026/27 spend forecast to $80bn/$100bn and introduces $125bn for 2028.

Based only on capacity under construction, US data center capacity rises from 65GW-gross in 2026 to 143GW-gross by 2030, with net additions of 33/37/8/0GW-gross in 2027/28/29/30. Texas is 20% of 2027E and 27% of 2028E net additions.
Consensus expects European EPS growth of 23% y/y in 3Q26, and most European sectors have seen positive 2026 EPS revisions since 30 September.
GS strategy raises its STOXX Europe 600 EPS growth forecast for this year to 18% and for 2027 to 7%, and introduces 5% for 2028. The historical average is 6.4%.
Technology is 43% of US earnings but 7% of European earnings. The ten largest US companies account for 40% of index earnings.

sector_views.rationale: Value has held up well in the US sell-off while growth and momentum factors sold off. This is described as observed performance, not a recommendation.
